title: Learn from experience
blurb: Explain how a PRINCE2 project seeks, records, acts on and shares lessons before, during and after the project.
question: A hospital trust is about to run its first ever robotics project. What does the 'learn from experience' principle expect the project management team to do at the start?

teach.body: Formally: a PRINCE2 project team actively seeks, records and implements improvements from lessons learned on earlier projects and throughout the current one, applies them in future projects and shares them so others can use them. In plain English: don't make the same mistake twice, repeat what worked, and pass it on.

items.label: Assess previous lessons: create the lessons log, review past lessons reports
Record lessons in the lessons log; share insights as you go
Review lessons; a lessons report may be produced
Evaluate the project; lessons report passed on to the business

teach.caption: Learning is continuous: it is not a single review at the end.

teach.h: From someone's experience to a better project

steps.label: Record
steps.sub: lessons log in the project log

teach.body: When a project is a 'first' for the business, or contains novel content, learning from others becomes even more important, including from people and organizations outside the business. Lessons come from successes as well as mistakes: many organizations repeat the same errors because nobody looked. And because much valuable knowledge is hidden in people's heads, social learning in a collaborative, knowledge-sharing environment matters as much as documents.

rows.label: Main use
values: Collect and act within the project

head: Practice
Lessons used for
rows: Shaping the team structure and a healthy project ecosystem
Improving the quality approach and product descriptions
teach.caption: Every practice draws on lessons; this is the principle applied day to day.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a first for the business
teach.body: Kestrel Valley Hospitals Trust has never deployed surgical robots. In starting up, project manager Grace Adeyemi creates the lessons log, reads lessons reports from the trust's last equipment roll-out and, because the work is new to the trust, arranges calls with two other hospitals that have done it. Midway, a team member finds a faster sterilization routine; Grace records it and shares it at a short team session. At closure, the lessons report goes to the trust's project office.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) learning only at the end; the principle applies before, during and after. (2) Mixing up products: lessons are collected in the lessons log and passed on in the lessons report. (3) In people questions, knowledge sharing and social learning point to learn from experience, while deciding at the most local level points to manage by exception.

items: Seek, record and act on lessons from prior projects and throughout this one; share them for others.
Starting up: 'assess previous lessons' creates the lessons log.
Novel or first-time projects: learning from others, including outside the business, matters even more.
Learn from successes as well as mistakes; share in ways that suit different learning needs.
At closure, the lessons report passes lessons on to the business.

summary: You can now explain how learn from experience is applied when starting, during and at the end of a project. You can also name the products involved: the lessons log to record lessons and the lessons report to pass them on.

A.q: Which statement describes the 'learn from experience' principle?
options: Lessons are sought, recorded, acted on and shared
Lessons are gathered by the business after closure
Lessons from mistakes are logged as project issues
Lessons are recorded at the final stage boundary
A.why: The project team actively seeks, records and implements lessons from prior projects and throughout the project, and shares them (manual 2.2).

whyNot.1: Lessons are sought from the very start, not just gathered after closure.
whyNot.2: Lessons go in the lessons log, and they come from successes as well as mistakes.
whyNot.3: Lessons are recorded throughout the project, not at one stage boundary.

A.q: In which process is the lessons log first created?
options: Initiating a project
Starting up a project
Controlling a stage
Directing a project
A.why: The 'assess previous lessons' activity in starting up a project creates the lessons log.

whyNot.0: Initiation completes the project log, but the lessons log already exists from starting up.
whyNot.2: Lessons are recorded during controlling a stage, but the log was created earlier.
whyNot.3: Directing a project is the board's process; it does not create the lessons log.

A.q: A project is the first of its kind for the organization. What does 'learn from experience' suggest?
options: Skip the lessons review, as no past projects match
Wait until the first stage ends to gather lessons
Seek lessons from others, including outside sources
Ask the project board to record lessons on its behalf
A.why: For a 'first' or novel project, it is even more important to learn from others, including external people and organizations.

whyNot.0: Lack of internal experience makes looking elsewhere more important, not less.
whyNot.1: Lessons are sought at the start, in starting up a project.
whyNot.3: The project manager owns the lessons log; the board does not record lessons for the project.

B.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. At the end of the project, lessons are passed on to the business in the [?].
options: lessons log
end stage report
daily log
lessons report
B.why: The lessons report passes lessons on so they can be applied on future projects; it is produced when evaluating the project in closing.

whyNot.0: The lessons log is the project's informal record, not the product that passes lessons on.
whyNot.1: The end stage report summarizes a stage for the board's next-stage decision.
whyNot.2: The daily log is the project manager's informal diary.

B.q:
Which two statements about learn from experience are correct?
1. Lessons can come from successes as well as mistakes.
2. Lessons are collected at closure to avoid disrupting delivery.
3. Social learning helps share knowledge that is hard to document.
4. Lessons are recorded in the issue register.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Lessons come from both mistakes and successes (1), and much knowledge is hidden in people and best shared through social learning (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: lessons are sought and recorded throughout, not held back to closure.
whyNot.2: Both are false: lessons are gathered throughout and kept in the lessons log.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: lessons belong in the lessons log, not the issue register.

B.q: A team manager finds a faster test method midway through a stage. How does the project best apply 'learn from experience'?
options: Record the lesson and share it with other teams now
Hold the lesson back for the end project report
Raise an exception report to the project board
Add the method to the risk register for review
B.why: Lessons are recorded and acted on throughout the project, and insights are shared as the project progresses.

whyNot.1: Waiting until closure loses the benefit for the rest of this project.
whyNot.2: Exception reports are for forecast breaches of tolerance, not for sharing lessons.
whyNot.3: The risk register holds risks; a lesson belongs in the lessons log.

C.q: Which activity and product apply 'learn from experience' at the very start of a project?
options: Assess previous lessons; lessons log
Evaluate the project; lessons report
Plan the initiation stage; daily log
Evaluate the stage; end stage report
C.why: In starting up a project, 'assess previous lessons' creates the lessons log and reviews lessons from similar projects.

whyNot.1: Evaluate the project and the lessons report belong to closing a project.
whyNot.2: Planning initiation is a starting up activity, but it does not create the lessons log.
whyNot.3: Evaluating the stage and the end stage report happen at a stage boundary.

C.q: Lessons from an earlier project show its estimates were 30% too low. Which practice most directly uses this lesson, and how?
options: Risk; by raising the risk appetite for this project
Quality; by adding extra quality review meetings
Plans; by improving the estimates for this project
Issues; by logging it as an off-specification
C.why: The plans practice uses lessons in estimating, so earlier under-estimates improve this project's estimates.

whyNot.0: Risk appetite is set by the business, not adjusted by an estimating lesson.
whyNot.1: Extra reviews do not address estimates being too low.
whyNot.3: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its specification, not a lesson.

C.q: When sharing lessons during the project, what does the principle ask the team to consider?
options: That lessons go to the project board first
That lessons are shared at closure in one report
That people have different learning needs
That lessons are kept within each team
C.why: As the project progresses, insights are shared, taking account of different learning needs and preferences.

whyNot.0: Lessons are shared widely across the project and beyond; there is no rule routing them to the board first.
whyNot.1: Sharing happens as the project progresses, not in one report at closure.
whyNot.3: The principle is about sharing lessons, not keeping them inside teams.

reteach.title: A recipe book that keeps improving
reteach.question: Think of a cook who notes what went wrong and right every time, reads others' notes first, and hands the book on. How does that match the principle?

blocks.body: Before cooking a new dish, a good cook reads other people's notes, especially for a dish they have never made. While cooking, they jot down what worked and adjust straight away. Afterwards, they tidy the notes and pass them on. A PRINCE2 project does the same: assess previous lessons in starting up, record and act on lessons in the lessons log during the project, then pass them on in a lessons report.

blocks.h: The same idea in PRINCE2 terms

blocks.text: Lessons are not only about mistakes, and not only collected at the end.

explain.body: In starting up a project, the 'assess previous lessons' activity creates the lessons log and draws on people and teams with experience of similar projects and on past lessons reports.

test.q: What does the 'assess previous lessons' activity produce?
options: The lessons report
The lessons log
The daily log
The issue register
test.why: Assess previous lessons, in starting up a project, creates the lessons log.

whyNot.0: The lessons report passes lessons on, typically at closure.
whyNot.2: The daily log is set up in starting up too, but it is the PM's diary, not the record this activity creates.
whyNot.3: The issue register is created in initiation.

explain.body: Lessons are recorded in the lessons log and acted on as the project goes: in estimates, plans, approaches and ways of working. Insights are shared with others as they arise.

test.q: Where are lessons recorded during the project?
options: The risk register
The issue register
The quality register
The lessons log
test.why: The lessons log, part of the project log, is the informal record of lessons.

whyNot.1: The issue register records formal issues.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and their results.

explain.body: When evaluating the project in closing, the project log is reviewed for lessons and a lessons report is produced so the business, and future projects, can benefit.

test.q: What is the purpose of the lessons report?
options: To pass on lessons for future use
To record the PM's daily notes
To request closure from the board
To confirm the users' acceptance
test.why: The lessons report passes on lessons that could be applied on this or future projects.

whyNot.1: Daily notes belong in the daily log.
whyNot.2: Closure is requested in the 'request project closure' activity, not by a lessons report.
whyNot.3: Acceptance is confirmed in 'confirm project acceptance'.

explain.body: Learn from successes as well as mistakes. For a first-of-a-kind project, seek lessons from outside the business. Much knowledge is hidden in people, so social learning matters.

test.q: Which statement about learn from experience is correct?
options: Lessons should come from failed projects
Successful approaches are also lessons
External lessons are outside its scope
Lessons are the board's responsibility
test.why: Lessons come from both mistakes and successes, to improve and innovate.

whyNot.0: Successes are a source of lessons too.
whyNot.2: Learning from external people and organizations is encouraged, especially for novel projects.
whyNot.3: The whole project team seeks and records lessons; the PM maintains the log.
